## TL;DR

The restart regression is addressed in the task branch and was already reviewed as good to go on pass 4. Detection now identifies renamed RepoOS processes running under systemd by inspecting the process cgroup and, when needed, the parent process command. Managed units are classified separately so the restart flow uses the service manager instead of signalling a process that systemd may respawn. The release notice reports progress and surfaces restart errors. The QA record explicitly says a real hand-run restart was not performed.

This resumed session found and cleared an unfinished Git merge left by a prior handoff attempt. The merge had all conflicts resolved but still had unrelated main changes staged; its finalization would have required a Git commit, which the current task instructions prohibit. `git merge --abort` restored the worktree to its prior state while retaining the existing task notes and unrelated task bookkeeping. No source files or the main checkout were changed in this resumed session.

## Work and rationale

The underlying issue was that a process title is not a reliable way to infer how a server started. A systemd user unit can launch a process whose command title is simply `repoos-<project>`, so detection needs to use supervisor metadata. The implementation first asks systemd about the PID. When that cannot identify a unit, it reads `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` for a service unit and then falls back to the parent process command. A recognized `com.repoos.serve.*` unit is treated as RepoOS-managed; an unrelated service unit is treated as externally supervised. If systemd is visible but the unit is not identifiable, the result is uncertain and automatic signalling is refused. This avoids treating a supervised server as hand-run and racing its automatic respawn.

On macOS, the existing launchd detection uses `launchctl list` and inspects relevant domains when the row is not in the caller's default listing. A hand-run process with an ordinary shell parent remains classified as hand-run. Tests exercise these distinctions, including the reported systemd parent command, cgroup discovery, launchd-managed processes, and shell-parented servers.

The update notice calls the restart endpoint for both managed and external supervisors. Its action enters a disabled “Restarting…” state after the server accepts the request; request failures and failure status are shown in the dialog. The notice also checks for the replacement server to return through the existing health/status flow. The progress and error states have preview fixtures and declared screenshots, which were captured successfully in the latest handoff according to the task record and review.

The QA document records that no real hand-run server restart was performed. That is important because automated detection and UI tests are not live restart evidence. No claim is made here that a hand-run, systemd, or launchd service was restarted during this resumed session.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the current branch state and the saved pass-4 review before changing anything. The review found no remaining bugs and specifically confirmed the restart screenshots and QA limitation. I reviewed the detector and tests around the new parent and cgroup paths, the restart decision logic, and the notice's progress/error handling. This showed the task's implementation was already present and did not need a speculative code change.

The previous handoff error came from an unfinished merge, not from an unresolved source conflict: `git status` reported all conflicts fixed, with a `MERGE_HEAD` present and numerous unrelated files staged. Because this session is instructed not to create commits, completing that merge was not an option. Aborting the merge returned Git to the original branch state and preserved the pre-existing unstaged worktree files. This also avoids bundling another task's changes into #1185.

## Challenges and blockers

The worktree contains pre-existing edits to several other task files and untracked task files. They are not part of #1185 and were left untouched. The task's own markdown contains RepoOS activity bookkeeping, and its newest review already records approval; I did not edit its status or attempt to commit it manually.

A real restart could not be verified in this session because no controlled hand-run server or supervised systemd/launchd instance was available. The QA note accurately records that limitation. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed: remote build and scoped tests completed, and the local format, lint, build freshness, contrast, and UI-smoke checks passed. The remote changed-path run expanded to 391 test files because the branch diff against `main` includes broader existing history; no test failure was reported.

## Key learnings

For Linux supervisor detection, process titles are insufficient evidence. PID status, cgroup membership, and parent process metadata provide complementary signals, and uncertain cases should remain uncertain rather than being treated as safe to signal. Distinguishing RepoOS's own managed unit from an external supervisor is also necessary because the correct restart mechanism differs.

The task's live restart acceptance cannot be inferred from screenshots or mocked API tests. The QA record therefore distinguishes UI and automated coverage from an actual operator restart. Finally, an unfinished merge can block RepoOS's partial checkpoint commit even when all conflicts are resolved; inspecting merge state before requesting handoff prevents confusing merge finalization with implementation failure.
